nodes.description: The Turkish NM_014722.2:c.102-1G>A allele causes exon 3 skipping in patient leukocyte RNA, producing p.Arg34_Asp86delinsSer, a net 52-residue deletion. The Tunisian NM_014722.4:c.1561C>T (p.Arg521*) allele is predicted to truncate RIPOR2 or reduce its abundance; patient protein absence and nonsense-mediated decay were not demonstrated. The proposed PX–BAR domain interpretation of the N-terminal deletion was challenged in published correspondence and remains unverified.

nodes.description: Taperin staining becomes reduced and diffuse in Ripor2-null hair cells, whereas espin staining is retained. No direct interaction with taperin, CLIC5, radixin, whirlin or the PTPRQ cytoplasmic domain was detected in the tested heterologous assays. RhoC enhances N-terminal RIPOR2 oligomerization in HEK293 cells, and tagged RhoC colocalizes with RIPOR2 in explants. The RL/AA construct fails rescue but also reduces basal homophilic binding, so it does not isolate a uniquely RhoC-dependent effect. A primary taper defect versus secondary disruption by abnormal bundle morphology remains unresolved.

P5 outer hair cells from Ripor2-null mice retain mechanically evoked currents, with reduced peak amplitude and a shifted, broadened displacement–open-probability curve. Mean saturated currents were approximately 233 pA in null cells and 417 pA in heterozygous controls. Re-expression in P2 explants restored fluid-jet-evoked GCaMP3 calcium responses; that rescue readout is not a direct measurement of restored transduction current.

nodes.description: RIPOR2 localizes around the basal stereociliary taper in mouse hair cells. Patient-deletion constructs accumulate in cytoplasmic inclusions in COS7 cells, and a related construct fails normal targeting in cultured mouse hair cells. These overexpression results support defective localization; they do not show endogenous mutant protein abundance or localization in the human cochlea. STORM ring geometry does not by itself establish direct lipid binding.

meta.association: Biallelic pathogenic RIPOR2 variants cause DFNB104. Reported alleles include NM_014722.2:c.102-1G>A, producing p.Arg34_Asp86delinsSer, and NM_014722.4:c.1561C>T (p.Arg521*). ClinVar RCV000190353 maps c.102-1G>A and NM_001286445.3:c.189-1G>A to the same genomic allele; these are transcript aliases, not independent variants. The distinct heterozygous c.1696_1707del (p.Gln566_Lys569del) allele causes DFNA21. In-frame deletion alone does not distinguish dominant from recessive disease; specific allele, segregation and phenotype must be considered.

nodes.description: Inner-hair-cell bundles are already severely disorganized at P2 in Ripor2-null mice; outer-hair-cell bundles initially retain much of their staircase arrangement but show orientation defects. By P5 both cell types have abnormal length, thickness or arrangement of stereocilia. Deterioration occurs during maturation. Little hair-cell loss is evident at P16/P28, so bundle pathology is not equivalent to early wholesale hair-cell death.
